sara: FYI found a reproducible hang when cancelling a typed async wrapper around client.stream(). It swallows aclose and leaves the server socket half-open. Repro attached.

sara: Short repro: declare wrapper as -> AsyncIterator[bytes], force a 401 mid-stream to trigger token refresh, then break the consumer loop. The server still shows connection ESTABLISHED and next requests stall.

sara: example:
```python
from typing import AsyncIterator

async def wrap(src: AsyncIterator[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    async for b in src:
        yield b.replace(b"x", b"y")

# consumer
async for chunk in wrap(client.stream("/v1/generate")):
    if stop_now:
        break
```

taylor: do you see SDK calling aclose() on its internal gen?

sara: SDK attempts to close, but our codebase creates a proxy wrapper (typing helpers) that doesn't forward aclose/athrow. So inner generator never gets closed.

ryan: two pieces: (1) user wrappers must preserve the async-iterator protocol including aclose, and (2) SDK could defensively try to find an inner generator to close when cancellation happens.

sara: quick workaround on app code: add try/finally around the async for and call await src.aclose() in finally. That fixes the leak.

alex: also saw similar with anyio/trio adapters where aclose raised CancelledError and the socket stayed open. We should swallow CancelledError on aclose and ensure socket teardown.

taylor: can you add a unit test that injects a 401 mid-stream and asserts aclose was awaited? will speed up triage.

sara: adding test + docs note about wrapper patterns. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/812

devex-bot: opened issue #3519 "py-sdk: typed proxy wrappers can drop aclose -> streaming cancel leak" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3519)

ryan: tagging eng-runtime + devex. happy to pair on a small runtime fallback to call inner.aclose() if wrapper lacks it.

sara: thanks — ping me tomorrow if you want to pair. :+1:
